name: Morocco
summary_text: Morocco is dangerous for trans visitors. Article 489 criminalises same-sex “indecent acts” (6 months–3 years), and Cairo 52 documents that trans people face de-facto criminalisation under Article 498 morality provisions — arrests based on gender-expression discrepancies and forced outing. The 2026 Cairo 52 report “A Web of Violence” describes a legal-medical-social system of erasure for trans people, including a de facto prohibition on transition care. Visitor-relevant cases exist: in 2024, Brazilian influencer Liziane Gutierrez was arrested in Marrakesh, accused by police of being transgender, and alleges she was forced to show her genitals — she spent a month in jail. In 2019, Marrakesh police filmed and humiliated a cross-dressing man after a traffic accident, leaking the video online. There is no LGR framework and police have wide discretion; tourist areas (Marrakesh, Agadir) are more tolerant in practice but the legal exposure is constant. The Gutierrez case demonstrates that even a cisgender visitor suspected of being trans can face genital inspection and jail.

sources.title: A Web of Violence: The Systemic Erasure of Transgender People in Morocco | Cairo 52 Legal Research Institute
sources.claim_summary: Cairo 52 report 'A Web of Violence: The Systemic Erasure of Transgender People in Morocco' (Jan 2026, by Hamzawya and Nora Noralla): based on interviews with 17 trans and non-binary Moroccans - documents an interlocking system of legal, medical, social and economic hostility; Morocco once pioneered gender-affirming surgery for foreigners but now enforces a de facto prohibition for its own citizens; Article 489 weaponised to arrest trans people based on gender expression; no legal gender recognition pathway.

sources.title: Morocco | Cairo 52 Legal Research Institute
sources.claim_summary: Cairo 52 country review of Morocco: no specific provisions on transition, but de facto criminalisation under Article 498 (moral charges, gender-expression discrepancies, involuntary outing); no gender-affirming healthcare framework, leading some to self-medicate; a 2021 recognition process exists for intersex people only; the Grand Mufti opposes transition.

sources.title: Instagram model alleges police in Morocco ‘forced her to show genitals’ over trans suspicions: Report | World News
sources.claim_summary: Hindustan Times (Nov 2024): an Instagram model alleges Moroccan police forced her to show her genitals over trans suspicions - reported police abuse of a trans woman based on appearance.

sources.title: Police abuse in Morocco: Moroccan police subject transvestite to online humiliation | Spain | EL PAÍS English
sources.claim_summary: El País (Jan 2019): Moroccan police subjected a Marrakesh cross-dresser to online humiliation - after a minor traffic accident, Chafiq was handcuffed and filmed by bystanders and police officers, who also photographed his ID documents and posted them online; he sought asylum in Europe. Homosexuality is punishable in Morocco.

sources.title: Morocco | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): Article 489 criminalises 'indecent acts' between persons of the same sex (6 months to 3 years) with wide police discretion and arbitrary arrests; 170 people charged with same-sex relations in 2018; HRW documented a 2020 campaign of online harassment of presumed gay and bisexual men; no legal gender recognition; public identification as LGBTIQ carries significant risk of violence and harassment; authorities block LGBTIQ organisations.

sources.title: Audacity in Adversity: LGBT Activism in the Middle East and North Africa | HRW
sources.claim_summary: HRW report (April 2018) 'Audacity in Adversity': LGBT activism in the Middle East and North Africa - includes Morocco's Article 489 criminalisation and the annex of laws used to punish same-sex conduct and gender expression across MENA.
ILGA 'State-Sponsored Homophobia' (May 2008, Daniel Ottosson): world survey of laws prohibiting same-sex activity between consenting adults - country-by-country legal survey including Morocco.

sources.title: U.N. Human Rights Council adopts LGBT resolution | Washington Blade
sources.claim_summary: Washington Blade (Sept 2014): the UN Human Rights Council adopted the SOGI resolution - international context for human-rights scrutiny of countries including Morocco.
